title: CounterNet: End-to-End Training of Prediction Aware Counterfactual Explanations

problem.claim: Counterfactual explanations seek the smallest feature modification that changes a machine-learning prediction to a predefined output.

gap.claim: Prior counterfactual-generation techniques are post-hoc, uninformed by model training, potentially misaligning predictions and explanations, and often require separate time-intensive optimization for each input.

contributions.claim: CounterNet is an end-to-end learning framework integrating predictive-model training and counterfactual-explanation generation in a single pipeline.
CounterNet optimizes counterfactual-explanation generation once together with the predictive model.
CounterNet is trained using a block-wise coordinate descent procedure.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe CounterNet as a novel departure from the prevalent post-hoc paradigm.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on multiple real-world datasets reportedly show high-quality predictions, 100% counterfactual validity for new input instances, and low proximity scores.
The authors report a well-balanced cost-invalidity trade-off.
The authors report that CounterNet runs 3X faster than existing state-of-the-art baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: The work presents CounterNet as an end-to-end framework integrating model training and counterfactual generation.
Counterfactual explanations are defined as minimal feature changes intended to produce a predefined prediction.
Existing approaches are characterized as post-hoc, potentially misaligned with model training, and computationally expensive per input.
CounterNet departs from the post-hoc paradigm, performs joint optimization once, and uses block-wise coordinate descent for training.
Experiments reportedly demonstrate prediction quality, counterfactual validity, proximity, trade-off, and runtime results.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the datasets, baselines, or experimental protocol.
The abstract does not define the reported proximity scores or cost-invalidity trade-off.
The abstract does not provide implementation details for the coordinate descent procedure.
